parts.model_answer:
To provide word-order/positional information, since self-attention alone does not
inherently encode the sequence order of tokens.
parts.text: Why is positional encoding required in transformers?

parts.model_answer:
Encoder-only models use bidirectional attention to understand input context,
mainly for tasks like classification and representation learning; decoder-only models use
causal (left-to-right) attention to predict the next token, mainly for text generation.
parts.text: What is the difference between encoder-only and decoder-only architectures?

parts.model_answer:
Masked attention prevents a token from attending to future tokens, ensuring
causal, left-to-right prediction. It is used in GPT-like models to prevent information
leakage during next-token prediction.
parts.text: What is masked attention and why is it used in GPT-like models?

(nucleus sampling) selects the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability
reaches p.
